title: quant-prefetch-buffer-corruption-incident-action-plan
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: During a traffic spike on 2025-02-17 we observed a regression in several production models using the int4 converter with the prefetch optimization enabled. Symptoms included elevated token-level error rates (accuracy drift) and intermittent crash loops on a subset of GPU hosts. The issue affected hosted customers on dedicated pools in us-west-2 and caused request failures and degraded outputs for ~6 hours before mitigation.
root_cause: An aggressive prefetch buffer reuse optimization accidentally allowed stale prefetch metadata to be reused across different model bindings when quantized weight shards were remapped at load time. The bug only manifested for int4-converted models with fragmented shard layouts and a specific cache eviction timing; it caused subtle corruption in the KV cache pointers. Corrupted KV pointers produced deterministic token mispredictions (accuracy drift) and periodically triggered a bounds-check abort in the runtime, causing crash loops on affected workers.
timeline:
2025-02-17 09:12 UTC - First elevated 5xx alerts from us-west-2 serving fleet.
2025-02-17 09:20 UTC - Automated rollback to model-variant v1.4 temporarily reduced errors but not fully.
2025-02-17 09:45 UTC - Engineering paged; initial hypothesis pointed to new int4 converter roll introduced two days prior.
2025-02-17 10:25 UTC - Mitigation: disabled prefetch optimization cluster-wide for dedicated pools in us-west-2. Error rate returned near baseline by 10:40 UTC.
2025-02-17 11:30 UTC - Root-cause repro branch created (git:github.com/redwood/runtime/prefetch-fix-repro).
2025-02-18 08:00 UTC - Hotfix PR opened and tested on canaries (PR #8421).
2025-02-20 14:00 UTC - Hotfix merged and staged to runtime-1.22-candidate.
2025-02-21 03:00 UTC - Rollout completed to affected fleets.
2025-02-25 16:00 UTC - Final validation and ticket creation for follow-ups.
impact_summary: Approximately 18 customer tenants saw increased token-level error rates (measured as mean token perplexity jump of ~12%) and ~2.3% of requests returned 5xx over a 6 hour window. No customer data was exfiltrated. The incident caused several high-traffic customers to trigger failover to fallback model variants; estimated revenue impact is low but developer time and SLA credits are expected for two enterprise customers.
mitigations:
Immediate: disabled prefetch optimization for int4-converted models in dedicated and hosted pools in us-west-2, and added runtime flag to force KV cache per-binding isolation.
Short-term: backported bounds-check guard and conservative pointer validation to runtime-1.22 branch and rolled to canaries.
Long-term: implement stronger invariant checks around prefetch metadata lifecycle, add fuzz tests for shard remapping scenarios, and extend canary matrix to include fragmented shard layouts and int4 model permutations.
postmortem_notes:
- Failure surfaced only under combined conditions: int4 converter + fragmented shard remap + prefetch enabled + specific eviction timing.
- Existing unit tests covered single-shard flows but not shard remap lifecycle.
- Code review gap: the prefetch change was fast-tracked to reduce startup latency and lacked a second-level runtime-safety review.
- Observability: there was insufficient telemetry that connected KV pointer validity to token-level accuracy metrics; added new metric proposal in action items.
- Communication: on-call runbook was followed; customers were notified within the SLA window but some follow-up customers requested a deeper RCA which this ticket will provide.
action_items: ENG-A1: Add pointer-integrity checks and defensive bounds guards to prefetch codepath (owner: Diego Martinez, estimate: 3, due: 2025-03-04)
ENG-A2: Backport hotfix to runtime-1.21 patch stream and stage to Dedicated fallback clusters (owner: Priya Nair, estimate: 2, due: 2025-02-28)
ENG-A3: Create fuzz-test harness for shard remap + int4 conversion permutations and add to CI (owner: Linh Tran, estimate: 5, due: 2025-03-11)
ENG-A4: Extend canary matrix to include fragmented-shard test models and run for 48 hours before auto-promote (owner: SRE Team, estimate: 2, due: 2025-03-07)

ENG-A5: Add token-level token-perplexity and kv-pointer-validity metrics to Console dashboards and create alert rule for abrupt token metric drift (owner: Data-Observability, estimate: 3, due: 2025-03-10)
ENG-A6: Postmortem writeup and customer communication pack (owner: Aisha Kapoor, estimate: 2, due: 2025-02-28)
ENG-A7: Add code-review checklist item for runtime-level safety for all performance optimizations (owner: Platforms Eng, estimate: 1, due: 2025-03-01)
ENG-A8: Run retrospective with int4 converter owners to evaluate rollback and gating policies for optimizer flags (owner: Connor Lee, estimate: 1, due: 2025-03-05)
notes: Customer follow-ups: Account team notified ACME Corp and NovaApps; follow-up meetings scheduled 2025-02-26 and 2025-02-27
Performance trade-off: disabling prefetch increases tail latency by ~3-6% for small-batch requests; will document exact cost impact in the hotfix PR notes
Acceptance criteria for closure: all action items resolved or triaged with owners, hotfix rolled to all impacted fleets, CI fuzz-tests green for 3 consecutive runs, and dashboard alerts in place
